4º de Primaria · Inglés · Tema 3

Questions with do and does

Nombre: ______________________   Fecha: ___________

Qué vas a aprender

  • Make yes/no questions with Do and Does (preguntas de sí o no)
  • Give short answers: Yes, I do / No, she doesn't
  • Ask open questions with what, where, when and what time
  • Interview a classmate about habits and likes

Para pensar

En español, para preguntar basta con cambiar la entonación: «¿Te gusta el chocolate?». ¿Funciona igual en inglés? ¿Se puede decir «You like chocolate?»

Explicación

The helper word do

In English, questions in the present simple need a helper word at the beginning: do. Look: «You like pizza.» → «Do you like pizza?». The helper goes first, then the person, then the verb.

En castellano: en español no tenemos esta palabra; solo ponemos los signos ¿? y cambiamos la voz. En inglés do no se traduce: es como una señal que avisa «¡atención, viene una pregunta!». Y recuerda que en inglés solo se escribe el signo de interrogación al final.

Do you…? Do they…?

We use Do with I, you, we and they: «Do you have a pet?», «Do we have English today?», «Do they live near the school?».

The verb stays in its normal form, the same as in the dictionary. These questions are perfect to know people: «Do you like football?», «Do you play an instrument?», «Do you speak French?». En castellano: «¿Tienes mascota?» se convierte en «Do you have a pet?». Fíjate en que el orden es distinto al español.

Does he…? Does she…?

With he, she and it the helper is Does: «Does your brother play basketball?», «Does she speak English?», «Does it rain a lot in London?».

Remember the rule of the -s: it goes to Does, so the verb doesn't have -s. We say «Does he play?», never «Does he plays?». It is the same trick as in negative sentences with doesn't. En castellano: la «s» viaja al ayudante y el verbo se queda limpio.

Short answers

To answer a yes/no question we don't repeat the whole sentence. We use a short answer with the same helper: «Do you like cats?» – «Yes, I do.» / «No, I don't.»

With does: «Does your mum cook?» – «Yes, she does.» / «No, she doesn't.». En castellano: en español contestamos «sí» o «no» solos, pero en inglés es más educado añadir la persona y el ayudante. Decir solo «Yes» no está mal, aunque suena un poco seco.

Question words

Some questions need more than yes or no. We use question words at the very beginning: What (qué), Where (dónde), When (cuándo), Who (quién), What time (a qué hora) and How (cómo).

The order is: question word + do/does + person + verb. «What do you eat for breakfast?», «Where does your cousin live?», «What time do you go to bed?». En castellano: es como poner primero el «¿qué?» o el «¿dónde?» y luego la pregunta normal con do.

Building an open question

Let's build a question step by step. We want to know the place where Sara lives. 1. Question word: Where. 2. Sara = she, so the helper is does. 3. Person: Sara. 4. Verb, normal form: live. Result: «Where does Sara live?»

The answer is a full sentence, not a short answer: «She lives in Toledo». Now the -s comes back to the verb, because there is no helper. Consejo: el ayudante aparece en la pregunta y desaparece en la respuesta.

Questions about you

These are very useful questions to meet a new friend. Learn them by heart: «What's your name?», «How old are you?», «Where do you live?», «What do you like?», «Do you have any brothers or sisters?», «What's your favourite colour?».

Some of these questions use the verb to be (am, is, are) and don't need do: «How old are you?», «Where is your school?». En castellano: el verbo to be es especial y no necesita ayudante; se pone delante de la persona. Lo demás va con do o does.

Reading: a pen friend

Read this email from Jack: «Hi Pablo! I'm Jack and I live in Manchester. Do you like sport? I love rugby. My sister Emma doesn't like sport, but she plays the violin. What do you do after school? I go swimming on Wednesdays. Does your school have a swimming pool? Mine doesn't. What time do you have lunch in Spain? We have lunch at twelve! Write soon, Jack.»

Find four questions in the text. Then answer them for Pablo: «Yes, I do», «I play basketball»…

Let's practise: class survey

Make a class survey (encuesta). Write five questions on a sheet: «Do you have a pet?», «Do you like vegetables?», «Do you play an instrument?», «What time do you get up?», «Where do you have lunch?». Ask five classmates and write their answers in a table.

At the end, tell the class one result with does or doesn't: «Marco has a pet. Inés doesn't have a pet». Consejo: cuando preguntes, mira a tu compañero, sonríe y di «Thank you!» al terminar.

Questions with do and does

Ejercicios

  1. Complete with Do or Does: «___ you like music?»

  2. Complete with Do or Does: «___ your dad cook?»

  3. Make a question: «They live in a flat.»

  4. Make a question: «Lucía has a bike.»

  5. Short answer (yes): «Do you play tennis?»

  6. Short answer (no): «Does your cat sleep a lot?»

  7. Translate: «¿Dónde vives?»

  8. Complete: «What time ___ she get up?»

  9. Correct: «Does he likes apples?»

  10. Write two questions for a new friend.

Practica

  1. «___ you have a brother?»

    1. A) Does
    2. B) Are
    3. C) Do

  2. «___ she like cats?»

    1. A) Does
    2. B) Do
    3. C) Is

  3. «Does he ___ football?»

    1. A) plays
    2. B) play
    3. C) playing

  4. Short answer: «Do you swim?» (yes)

    1. A) Yes, I swim.
    2. B) Yes, I do.
    3. C) Yes, I does.

  5. Short answer: «Does Tom cook?» (no)

    1. A) No, he don't.
    2. B) No, he not.
    3. C) No, he doesn't.

  6. «Where» means…

    1. A) dónde
    2. B) cuándo
    3. C) qué

  7. «___ time do you get up?»

    1. A) When
    2. B) Where
    3. C) What

  8. Which question is correct?

    1. A) Where she lives?
    2. B) Where does she live?
    3. C) Where do she live?

  9. Which question doesn't need do?

    1. A) How old are you?
    2. B) Do you like rice?
    3. C) What do you eat?

  10. In English the question mark goes…

    1. A) only at the end
    2. B) at the start and the end
    3. C) only at the start

Explícalo con tus palabras

Incluye: Para qué sirve el ayudante do en las preguntas; Cuándo se usa do y cuándo does; Cómo se dan respuestas cortas; Cómo se forma una pregunta con where, what o what time.

Resumen

Tarjetas de repaso

Recórtalas: pregunta delante, respuesta detrás.

Do you…?Pregunta con I, you, we, they.
Does she…?Pregunta con he, she, it.
Yes, I do.Respuesta corta afirmativa.
No, he doesn't.Respuesta corta negativa.
WhatQué.
WhereDónde.
What timeA qué hora.
?En inglés, solo al final de la pregunta.

Soluciones

  1. C) you + Do.
  2. A) she + Does.
  3. B) Tras Does, sin s.
  4. B) Respuesta corta.
  5. C) he + doesn't.
  6. A) Where = dónde.
  7. C) What time = a qué hora.
  8. B) Wh- + does + persona + verbo.
  9. A) To be no usa do.
  10. A) Solo ? al final.

Soluciones de los ejercicios

  1. Do.
  2. Does.
  3. Do they live in a flat?
  4. Does Lucía have a bike?
  5. Yes, I do.
  6. No, it doesn't.
  7. Where do you live?
  8. does.
  9. Does he like apples?
  10. Model answer: Do you have any pets? What do you do after school?
